advisor_identified: Douglas Neil Sprague, historian in the University of Manitoba History Department and supervisor of the listed 1995 thesis.

evidence.says: The acknowledgements of In Order to Live Untroubled identify the thesis advisor as Professor D.N. Sprague of the University of Manitoba History Department.
The author note for Canada and the Métis, 1869-1885 identifies D.N. Sprague as teaching history at the University of Manitoba since 1971.
The library catalogue names Douglas Neil Sprague as the author of Canada and the Métis, 1869-1885, establishing the full name of the Manitoba historian.
David Library of the American Revolution, Dissertations on Microfilm, page 30, lists Douglas Neil Sprague, The American Revolution: An Explanation, University of Washington, Seattle, 1971 (film 118).

The bibliography lists Sprague, Douglas N., The American Revolution: an explanation (1971), as a Ph.D. thesis at the University of Washington; it also cites Dissertation Abstracts International 32A, November 1971, page 2623.

notes: The linked title, institution and year match both dissertation bibliographies. Identification as the advisor is inferred from the matching full name established through the Manitoba historian’s book catalogue record; no CV directly stating his doctorate was located.
